conviction_note: Q3 numbers are new and Hexagon's results days move a lot (13.7%, 16.8%, 13.3%, 11.8% on four of the last six reports), so abs_move is 8.5. But everything I found is either inside the raised FY26 guide of about NOK 300m EBITDA (the Certarus Mobile Pipeline ramp), a soft proxy (Cummins' stronger US heavy-duty truck market, which is mostly diesel pre-buy), or a below-EBITDA one-off (likely a fair-value loss on the Hexagon Purus convertible bond). p_up therefore sits at 52 and the findings sum to +0.1.

already_public.what: FY2026 EBITDA guidance raised from above NOK 200m to around NOK 300m; H1 EBITDA NOK 126m, so H2 implies about NOK 174m (about 87 a quarter against 69 in Q2)
Certarus Mobile Pipeline order, about USD 100m (about NOK 1bn), deliveries starting Q3 2026, most of it over the following 12 months
IVECO BUS exclusive 3-year LTA; 2026 IVECO revenue estimated at EUR 20m
Hexagon Purus Q3: EBITDA NOK -83m, equity NOK -224m, financial restructuring incl. the convertible bonds under discussion
Q3 date and time confirmed by the issuer: 6 Nov 2026, 07:00 CET, webcast 08:30 CET

new_in_release.expect: Q3 EBITDA against an implied run-rate of about 87m and Mobile Pipeline revenue against Q2's 101m as Certarus deliveries begin. Direction unknown; the bar is unsourced

FY26 'around NOK 300m' reiterated is most likely. The company flagged 'risks ... in terms of the timing and execution of order deliveries', so a trim is the tail risk. Any first 2027 colour is two-sided upside
The Certarus ramp probably builds inventory and receivables. Free cash flow could disappoint even on a good EBITDA. Unknown
Fair-value loss on the Hexagon Purus convertible bond (NOK 131m at 30 June) and any Hexagon role in the Purus restructuring. Negative, below EBITDA

positioning_check: Finanstilsynet SSR register read as of 2026-11-04: no disclosed net short at or above 0.5% (https://ssr.finanstilsynet.no/api/v2/instruments). anchor_covered is false, so this is the truncation floor and not a measurement, and the lean (+0.52) is the run-up term only. JPMorgan Chase has crossed 5% back and forth four times in October (5.095% on 8 Oct, 4.934% on 15 Oct, 5.001% on 20 Oct, 5.265% on 27 Oct), which looks like prime-broker or stock-lending flow (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=685083).

findings.finding: The USD 100m Certarus Mobile Pipeline order was due to start delivering in Q3 2026. The company said North American Mobile Pipeline volumes 'are expected to pick up significantly in the second half', from Q2 segment revenue of only NOK 101m, so Q3 should be the first quarter carrying the ramp the raised FY guide rests on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EBITDA beat (69 against a DNB Carnegie-cited consensus of 43) plus the guide raise: +13.65%. Q3 2025 miss: -16.84%. The stock has given back the whole Q2 move (14.50 on 14 Aug to 10.85 on 5 Nov) without any company news
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the order and the guide are public, and the ramp sits inside the company's own guidance, so this finding goes toward 0. The only unpriced part is whether deliveries actually started on time. A market confident of the ramp would not have marked the stock down 24% over 60 days after a raise.
findings.independence: Superior Plus (Certarus' parent) said on its Q2 call that Houston would begin gas flow in Q3 2026 (search snippet, https://stockanalysis.com/quote/tsx/SPB/transcripts/). It reports Q3 only on 10 Nov, after the window

findings.finding: Cummins' Q3 2026 release (5 Nov) shows North American heavy-duty engine shipments of 33,200 against 22,400 a year earlier and 30,100 in Q2, and says 'the U.S. medium- and heavy-duty truck markets strengthened'. This is a soft read-through to Hexagon Agility's truck fuel systems, which go on the Cummins X15N.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable: truck was about NOK 105m of Q2 Fuel Systems revenue of 450m
findings.why_not_priced: Released the day before the print, so it is only partly in the price (HEX was -1.4% on 5 Nov). But the strength is mostly diesel pre-buy ahead of EPA 2027, which Hexagon itself said keeps natural gas truck volumes 'at moderate levels'. Transmission is a hypothesis, and the net of the rest of the company (Mobile Pipeline, bus) dominates.
findings.independence: Hexagon's Q2 outlook expected H2 truck volumes to improve on H1 (same Q2 report URL as finding 1). It is the company's own statement, so it is not independent

findings.finding: Hexagon Purus, 34.6% owned and carried at zero, fell from about NOK 12 at end-June to about NOK 4.3 at end-September, reported negative equity of NOK -224m and opened a restructuring 'including measures relating to the outstanding convertible bonds'. Hexagon carried a Purus convertible bond at a Level-3 fair value of NOK 131m at 30 June, so a Q3 fair-value loss below EBITDA is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Purus impairments in 2025 (NOK -268m) sat inside large down days, but they came with operating misses and cannot be separated out
findings.why_not_priced: The Purus collapse is public, and the write-down is non-cash and below EBITDA with no path to the guide. What the market has not seen is how much of the NOK 131m goes, and whether Hexagon is asked to convert or extend under the restructuring. The Q2 report says Hexagon has 'no legal or constructive obligation to fund the associate further'.
findings.independence: Q2 report note: 'Convertible bond at fair value ... 131 216' and the equity stake 'reduced to zero' (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/attachment?messageId=679113&attachmentId=330510). Purus price series: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HPUR.OL?range=6mo&interval=1wk

findings.finding: JPMorgan Chase crossed the 5% threshold in Hexagon four times in October through J.P. Morgan Securities PLC (5.265% on 27 Oct). The Norwegian short register shows no disclosed net short at or above 0.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: A prime-broker holding that oscillates around 5% usually reflects lent-out stock or client swaps, not a directional bet. It could hide several sub-0.5% shorts, but nothing here signs it, so it is filed at 0.
findings.independence: Finanstilsynet SSR: no position at or above 0.5% as of 2026-11-04 (https://ssr.finanstilsynet.no/api/v2/instruments)

baseline_tension: The lean is a small positive (+0.52, from the -10.5% 20-day run-up) and my findings are near-flat (+0.1). Nothing cuts against the lean; the 24% de-rating since the guide raise without company news reads as lowered expectations, but it is an unexplained drawdown and worth 0.
language_note: Nothing the English sources did not already carry: Hexagon publishes every release in English on NewsWeb, and Norwegian searches (aksje, tredje kvartal forventninger, Finansavisen) returned only English releases or older DNB Carnegie notes. The DNB Carnegie Norwegian note of 6 Aug 2026 ('Tilsvarende konsensus ligger på henholdsvis NOK 709 mill., NOK 43 mill.', i.e. 'the corresponding consensus is NOK 709m and NOK 43m respectively') gave the only sourced bar for Q2, and no Q3 equivalent was found
lessons_applied: The Certarus ramp lands inside the company's own guide, so that finding went from +0.4 to +0.2
Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis: the Cummins read-through went from +0.2 to +0.1
A one-off below operating income is sized at a fraction: the Purus convertible bond went from -0.3 to -0.2

Size the move on what is new and do not cap it at history: abs_move_pct went from 8.0 to 8.5 (new numbers, a possible guide change, HEX's own double-digit results days, 7-analyst coverage at $1.2m/day)
Verified fact is not a reaction, and Q3 has historically been HEX's worst print: p_up went from 53 to 52
Cash can outweigh the guide: working capital on the ramp is added as an unknown line in new_in_release
